### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. neuronopathy, distal hereditary motor, type 2A  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.779)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3371571)

**Proposed mechanism:** HSPB8 (HGNC:30171) —DISRUPTS→ Protein homeostasis and cellular stress response (GO:0031379); Protein homeostasis and cellular stress response (GO:0031379) —LEADS_TO→ Peripheral neuropathy (HP:0003489); Protein homeostasis and cellular stress response (GO:0031379) —LEADS_TO→ Distal muscle weakness (HP:0002460). Haploinsufficiency of HSPB8 disrupts protein homeostasis and cellular stress response pathways, which in turn leads to the development of peripheral neuropathy and distal muscle weakness characteristic of both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in HSPB8 with a population frequency greater than 1% in gnomAD. _(variant: HGVS:c.X_Y_Z)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of HSPB8 in protein homeostasis offers potential therapeutic targets for both conditions, such as strategies aimed at enhancing chaperone activity or improving protein clearance mechanisms.

#### 2. myopathy, myofibrillar, 13, with rimmed vacuoles  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.733)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3371571)

**Proposed mechanism:** HSPB8 (HGNC:30171) —DISRUPTS→ Intermediate filament organization and dynamics (GO:0007010); Intermediate filament organization and dynamics (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Peripheral neuropathy (HP:0003489); Intermediate filament organization and dynamics (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324). Mutations in HSPB8 disrupt intermediate filament organization and dynamics, leading to both peripheral neuropathy (Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease axonal type 2L) and muscle weakness (myopathy, myofibrillar, 13, with rimmed vacuoles).

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in HSPB8 that do not disrupt intermediate filament organization and dynamics, or variants with a demonstrably different functional consequence in the two disease contexts. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the downstream effects of HSPB8 dysfunction on intermediate filament dynamics could offer therapeutic strategies for both conditions.

#### 3. isolated focal cortical dysplasia type II  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.458)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3371571)

**Proposed mechanism:** HSPB8 (HGNC:24128) —DISRUPTS→ Protein aggregation (GO:0051014); Protein aggregation (GO:0051014) —LEADS_TO→ Autophagy-lysosome pathway (GO:0000277); Autophagy-lysosome pathway (GO:0000277) —LEADS_TO→ Axonal degeneration (HP:0003489); TSC1 (HGNC:11714) —DISRUPTS→ mTOR signaling pathway (GO:0035556); TSC2 (HGNC:11715) —DISRUPTS→ mTOR signaling pathway (GO:0035556); mTOR signaling pathway (GO:0035556) —DECREASES→ Autophagy-lysosome pathway (GO:0000277); Autophagy-lysosome pathway (GO:0000277) —LEADS_TO→ Focal cortical dysplasia (HP:0030051). Mutations in HSPB8 lead to impaired protein degradation, causing protein aggregation and subsequent axonal degeneration in CMT2L. In FCDII, mutations in TSC1/TSC2 disrupt the mTOR pathway, which in turn impairs the autophagy-lysosome pathway. This impaired autophagy can lead to accumulation of misfolded proteins and cellular dysfunction, contributing to the characteristic cortical dysplasia.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a common genetic variant in HSPB8 or components of the autophagy-lysosome pathway with a high allele frequency (>1%) in gnomAD, which would suggest it is not pathogenic for either disease. _(variant: rs141009650)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the autophagy-lysosome pathway or modulating protein aggregation could offer therapeutic strategies for both Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2L and focal cortical dysplasia type II, suggesting a shared therapeutic target despite distinct primary genetic causes.
